clue.text: I eat under the moon

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one word under another simply means it follows it in the grid

parts.note: Io is one of the moons of Jupiter
to dine is to eat

explanation.surface: Someone describing a romantic meal taken outdoors by moonlight.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'I' reads as the speaker but is the definition: I is the chemical symbol for iodine.
explanation.definitionFit: In the periodic table, the element iodine carries the single-letter chemical symbol I.

clue.text: Scruff has shag, perhaps, before writing letter ending romance

indicators.note: one piece is placed ahead of the other in the entry

parts.note: shag is a long, rough pile on cloth or carpet, an example of a nap

indicators.note: the written letter that ends a word is its final one, so only that is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: A scruffy character with a shag haircut writing the final letter of a love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: Shag is not hair here but a rough woolly pile on fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: The scruff is the back of the neck, the same body part a nape names.

clue.text: Artfully hide returning fat with particular angle

indicators.note: something returning goes back the way it came, so this word is read backwards
doing something artfully means arranging it with cunning, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of hide rearranged
lard is pig fat used in cooking

explanation.surface: Cunningly concealing some fat while one works at a certain angle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide' looks like a verb working with 'artfully', and it is the anagram fodder; 'particular angle' is the definition, a technical term from geometry and aircraft design.
explanation.definitionFit: A dihedral is the specific angle formed where two planes meet, such as the upward tilt of aircraft wings.

clue.text: Scandal in America not fully written up in paper

indicators.note: in a down entry, writing upwards means the run of letters is read from the bottom
the words are not used fully, only a run of letters lying across them

parts.note: the letters running from the end of scandal through in to the start of America

explanation.surface: A political scandal in the USA only partly reported in a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Paper' looks like a newspaper in the surface; it is the definition, a type of strong brown paper.
explanation.definitionFit: Manila is a strong buff-coloured paper, originally made from Manila hemp, used for envelopes and folders.

clue.text: Mince pie at work? Can't wait for this!

indicators.note: letters set to work are busy moving about, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these three words used together

explanation.surface: Someone at the office eyeing a Christmas mince pie and unable to hold off eating it.
explanation.walkthrough: A mince pie is a small British Christmas pastry filled with dried fruit. The whole clue also describes the eager feeling.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unable to wait is exactly the state of restlessness and eagerness that this noun names.

clue.text: Stringed instruments inlaid with ten inverted horseshoes

indicators.note: something inlaid is set into another material, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: lutes are plucked stringed instruments

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down entry, so the number word is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Musical instruments decorated with ten upside-down horseshoes for luck.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'inverted' means read upwards; the horseshoes are the definition, not decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: A lunette is anything crescent-shaped, including a kind of light, half-moon horseshoe.

clue.text: In a scrum, I am shown to be unmanly

indicators.note: a rugby scrum is a heaving jumble of bodies, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A rugby player revealed in the scrum as not tough enough.
explanation.definitionFit: Womanish is an old-fashioned, usually disparaging adjective for a man thought effeminate or lacking manliness.

clue.text: Are cards kept close to the chest in these talks? On the contrary

parts.words: Are cards kept close to the chest in these talks?
parts.note: surface reading: secretive negotiations where players hide their hands
setter's reading: the opposite holds, the cards of one red suit held close to the organ inside the chest, an open and frank exchange

explanation.surface: Wondering whether negotiators in certain talks are being secretive.
explanation.walkthrough: Keeping cards close to the chest means being secretive; these talks are the opposite, open and sincere. The setter also puns on cards of the suit being held to the organ in one's chest.
explanation.definitionFit: These are intimate, candid conversations in which people speak openly about personal feelings.

clue.text: Toxic husband falling out is all she can bear

indicators.note: something falling out drops away, so this letter is removed from the word

parts.note: toxic means harmful
H is the abbreviation for husband

explanation.surface: A wife who has fallen out with a poisonous husband and can take no more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'All she can bear' sounds like endurance, but it means what she can physically carry.
explanation.definitionFit: An armful is the quantity a person can hold in their arms, so the most she can carry.

clue.text: Nation of characters remarkable in their eloquence

indicators.note: the solver is told some letters are notable within the following words, so they are found lying there

parts.note: letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: Praise for a nation of people famous for their gift of the gab.
explanation.walkthrough: The Irish are famed for eloquence, so the surface points at the answer too.
explanation.definitionFit: Eire is the Irish-language name for Ireland, the independent republic and country.

clue.text: Roots out drug issues involving cocaine

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: something that radiates sends out or issues
C is slang shorthand for cocaine

explanation.surface: A police operation tackling drug problems, cocaine in particular.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' looks like a noun, problems, but it is the verb meaning gives out. C goes inside RADI-ATES after E.
explanation.definitionFit: To eradicate is to destroy completely, literally to pull up by the roots.

clue.text: Maybe fire her over lunch?

indicators.note: one piece is spread over the other, covering it on both sides

parts.note: taken as written
to lunch is to eat

explanation.surface: A boss wondering whether to sack an employee during a lunch meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fire' suggests dismissal, but it is a gas or electric fire, an example of the answer, hence 'Maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fire in a room, gas or electric, is one example of an appliance that warms the air.

clue.text: Deal with marriage organisation that improves relations

parts.note: to deal is to trade
a marriage is a union

explanation.surface: Settling a matter connected with a wedding, through an agency that brings people closer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Relations' suggests family; here it means industrial relations between workers and employers.
explanation.definitionFit: A union of workers bargains with employers to improve pay and conditions, the employer-employee relationship.

clue.text: Passionate about putting career first? Rubbish

indicators.note: the second idea is placed first in the entry, ahead of the other piece

parts.note: to career is to rush headlong, to tear along
being into something means being keen on it

explanation.surface: A sceptic dismissing someone who claims to love work-first ambition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Career' looks like a noun, a working life; it is the verb meaning to dash. 'Rubbish' is the verb, to criticise harshly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rubbish someone is to criticise them scathingly, and to tear into them is to attack verbally.

clue.text: Properties of underwear that will inspire cuddling

indicators.note: to inspire is literally to breathe in, so one piece takes the other inside it

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underwear
cuddling someone is holding them

explanation.surface: Lingerie advertising promising its wearer will be embraced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Properties' looks like qualities of the underwear; it means pieces of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Smallholdings are small agricultural plots of land, each one a property that can be owned or rented.

clue.text: Ring Tusk about avoiding borders (never ending like a circle)

indicators.note: avoiding the borders means leaving off the outer letters of the word
turned about, the remaining letters are read in the other direction

parts.note: the word with its first and last letters dropped

indicators.note: the ending of the word is its final letter alone

parts.note: the final letter of the word
a circle is round

explanation.surface: Instructions for encircling an elephant's tusk with a never-ending ring.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed words look like an aside about the ring; they are wordplay, the end of 'never' and a word for circular.
explanation.definitionFit: To ring something is to encircle or enclose it completely, which is what surround means as a verb.

clue.text: Dutch is right — say it isn't so!

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for Dutch
taken as written
a right to something is a claim on it

explanation.surface: The setter, Dutch, insisting he is correct and urging others to deny something.
explanation.walkthrough: Dutch is the setter's own pseudonym, so the surface seems to be about him.
explanation.definitionFit: To disclaim is to deny or renounce, refusing to accept that something is true or belongs to you.

clue.text: Time to regret being grounded in reality

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for time
to rue is to regret
being, existence, is life

explanation.surface: A sobering moment of remorse that brings someone back down to earth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being grounded' reads as one phrase, but 'being' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A true-life story is one based on actual events rather than fiction, hence rooted in reality.

clue.text: Is the contracted motorway to provide narrow junctions?

indicators.note: a contracted word is shortened, here losing its last letter

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, its 1 read as the letter I

explanation.surface: Asking whether a shortened stretch of motorway will create tight interchanges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Junctions' suggests motorway exits, but these are strips of land joining two larger land masses.
explanation.definitionFit: Isthmi, plural of isthmus, are narrow necks of land that join two larger areas.

clue.text: Muslim ruler apparently not as loud as western lawman

indicators.note: less loud means without the musical symbol for loudness, so that letter goes

parts.note: a sheriff is the law officer of the Wild West

explanation.surface: Comparing a quiet Islamic ruler with a noisy Wild West lawman.
explanation.walkthrough: F is forte, the musical term for loud; one F comes out of SHERIFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A sherif or sharif is a title for an Arab or Muslim ruler or noble descended from the Prophet.

clue.text: SI unit for movement in designated position

indicators.note: the letters are given room to move, so they shift into a new order

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A physics note about the international unit used to measure motion.
explanation.definitionFit: In situ is Latin for in its original or proper place, so located exactly where intended.

clue.text: Forced Widdecombe, on making a comeback, to join loony ultra

indicators.note: coming back means going in the opposite direction, so these words are read backwards

parts.note: Ann Widdecombe is a former Conservative MP, followed by on as written

indicators.note: a loony is crazy, so the letters are scrambled

parts.note: the letters of ultra rearranged

explanation.surface: A politician making a comeback is pushed into alliance with an extremist.
explanation.walkthrough: Ann Widdecombe is an outspoken British politician who made a comeback as a Brexit Party MEP; ANN plus ON reversed gives NONNA.
explanation.definitionFit: Non-natural describes something artificial or contrived, as forced behaviour is strained and unnatural.

clue.text: Blue sky sometimes is unavailable

indicators.note: only some of the time, so every other letter is taken

parts.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A weather remark about clear skies being a rare commodity.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone occupied with other things cannot be reached or seen, so they are engaged and not free.

clue.text: On the mend, abstainer rejected drink

indicators.note: something rejected is thrown out, so these letters are removed

parts.note: someone on the mend is getting better
TT, teetotal, marks someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A recovering teetotaller turns down an alcoholic drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the abstainer from BETTER leaves the drink: a neat irony.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer is an alcoholic drink brewed from malted grain and hops.

clue.text: Where students learn to sing?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: in a school class, a form in British schools
second meaning: to grass, give information to the police

explanation.surface: A question about where pupils have singing lessons.
explanation.walkthrough: A form is a British school class, so students learn in form. To sing is underworld slang for informing on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it places pupils in their class; as one, it means telling the police about others.

clue.text: Tilt toes to fit this?

indicators.note: the letters must be adjusted so they fit, so they are rearranged

parts.note: the letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Advice on cramming your feet into a steep high-heeled shoe.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: wearing a stiletto heel tips the toes downward.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a woman's shoe with a very high, thin heel that pitches the foot forward.
